{{short description|Japanese primatologist and anthropologist (b. 1952)}}
{{Expand Japanese|topic=bio|長谷川眞理子|date=April 2023}}
'''Mariko Hiraiwa Hasegawa''' ({{langx|ja|長谷川眞理子}}, born 1952) is a Japanese zoologist and anthropologist who studies behavioral ecology, evolutionary psychology, and physical anthropology.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Mariko Hasegawa {{!}} Center for Academic Research and Training in Anthropogeny (CARTA) |url=https://carta.anthropogeny.org/users/mariko-hasegawa |access-date=2023-04-23 |website=carta.anthropogeny.org |language=en}}</ref> Hasegawa served as the president of the [[The Graduate University for Advanced Studies|Graduate University for Advanced Studies]] (Sokendai) in [[Kanagawa Prefecture]], Japan, until 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mariko Hasegawa, Ph.D CV 2001 |url=https://www.jsps.go.jp/file/storage/general/english/e-toplevel/data/07_committee/2021/03_Hasegawa_2021.pdf}}</ref> She is "among the rare Japanese women primatologists to have gained international recognition."<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Herzfeld |first=Chris |title=The great apes : a short history |date=2017 |others=Kevin Frey, Jane Goodall |isbn=978-0-300-22137-4 |location=New Haven |page=250 |oclc=982651819}}</ref>

Her mother Satsue Mito collected field data on Japanese macaque troupes beginning in the 1950s, ultimately documenting four decades worth of behavior. Mito documented the cultural transmission of sweet-potato-washing within a group of wild macaques.<ref name=":0" /> During Hasegawa's doctoral studies at the [[University of Tokyo]], she also studied Japanese macaques, as well as Tanzanian chimpanzees.<ref name=":1" /> She won a [[British Council Scholarship]] and went to [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]] for zoology.<ref name=":1" /> She was on the faculty of [[Senshu University]] from 1990 to 2000, at which time she joined the faculty of [[Waseda University]].<ref name=":1" />
